newsitem.title: USA: World Bank sees debt initiative cases by year - end.
newsitem.headline: World Bank sees debt initiative cases by year - end.

text.p: World Bank President James Wolfensohn said Friday he expected to see debt-laden countries assisted under the IMF-World Bank debt initiative by the end of the year.

In a press conference in conjunction with the IMF-World Bank annual meeting, Wolfensohn said he believed that the international authorities, including the Paris Club, would work together on a case-by-case basis to get this program underway.
"My guess is that between now and the end of the year we will have our first cases," Wolfensohn said.
Wolfensohn added, "I think we're very close to reaching a positive and productive agreement that will allow us to proceed immediately on specific cases."
He said he understood that a consensus was emerging at the Paris Club of official creditors that would allow the debt initiative to proceed on a "case-by-case basis."

Asked about whether the Paris Club had agreed to forgive 80 percent of its loans to specific countries, Wolfensohn said he did not know whether it was 80 percent, but he did not think it was 90 percent as the bank and IMF had been recommending.

The bank has already committed a $500 million war chest to the program, and Wolfensohn repeated that he was prepared to recommend to the World Bank board that it commit a total $2 billion over the years ahead.
